title: Missed Call Text Back: video sales letter

slides.title: It's 9 PM. The *phone rings*. *Nobody answers.*
slides.sub: What one unanswered call can cost a home service company
slides.narration: Picture this. It's nine o'clock at night, and a homeowner has water coming through the ceiling. They grab their phone, search for a plumber, and call the first name they see. It rings. And rings. Nobody picks up. They're not going to leave a voicemail. They've got water coming through the ceiling. So they hang up, and call the next company on the list. And you'd never even know it happened.

slides.title: What was on the *other end* of that call?
slides.note: Examples of large jobs by trade. Actual job values and outcomes vary.
slides.narration: Here's what makes that so painful. That call wasn't a two hundred dollar service visit. Depending on your trade, it could have been a twelve thousand dollar repipe. A fifteen thousand dollar H V A C system. A thirty thousand dollar roof. Even a water loss job worth a hundred thousand. And the big jobs don't wait for business hours. They show up at the worst possible time, from people who need an answer right now.

slides.label: of calls go *unanswered*, even at businesses that list *24/7 hours*
slides.note: Based on OnCall Local's after-hours calls to home service businesses listing 24/7 hours. Sample: N = ___ calls, ___ to ___. DRAFT: confirm before use.
slides.narration: Now, you might be thinking, I'm covered, my phone's on twenty-four seven. Here's what we've found. Among home service businesses that list their hours as twenty-four seven, thirty-eight percent of calls go unanswered. And that's not because those owners don't care. It's because everyone misses calls. Period.

slides.title: Why calls get missed

cards.p: Under a sink, on a roof, or with another customer.
Dinner, family time, or asleep at two in the morning.

slides.narration: Think about your day. You're under a sink, up on a roof, or in the middle of a job with another customer. Or you're finally sitting down to dinner. Even companies with a team answering the phones around the clock still miss calls. Nobody can pick up every single one. So let's look at what actually happens when a call gets missed.

slides.note: Illustration only. Not a real customer or call.
slides.narration: Here's the customer's side of it. They search. They find you. They tap call. It rings, and nobody answers. So they go back to the list, tap the next company, and that company picks up. Just like that, the job is gone, before you ever knew it existed.

slides.note: Illustration only. Not a real customer or call.
slides.narration: Now watch the same moment with missed call text back. They tap call. Nobody answers. But right before they tap the next company, a text pops up from your business. Sorry we missed your call, how can we help? The conversation has started, and it started with you.

slides.narration: And this isn't theory. One of our clients is Discount Plumbing, in Northern California. They already have their own employees answering the phones twenty-four seven, three sixty-five. And still, calls slipped through. With missed call text back running behind their team, they've sold over eighty-three thousand dollars in jobs this year. Work that might have gone to the next plumber on the list.

slides.title: How *missed call text back* works
items: The caller gets a *text from your business* in seconds
An *assistant* finds out who they are and what they need
You get the *whole conversation*, and you *call back first*
slides.note: The text assistant is an AI and introduces itself as your business's virtual assistant.
slides.narration: So how does it work? When a call goes unanswered, the caller gets a text from your business within seconds. A virtual assistant asks what's going on and gets the details. Then you get the whole conversation on your phone, and you call them back first.

slides.text: You don't have to answer *every* call. You just have to be the *first to respond*.
slides.narration: And that's really the whole idea. These customers aren't waiting around. They're shopping, right now. A text starts the conversation while they're still deciding who to hire. You don't have to answer every call. You just have to be the first to respond.

slides.title: What you need to do

cards.p: Everything is set up in your account for you.
Your calls forward after a few rings if you don't pick up.
Read the conversation, then call the customer.

slides.narration: The best part is, there's nothing for you to build. We set everything up inside your account. You keep your own phone number. If you don't pick up after a few rings, the call forwards, and the text goes out. All you do is read the conversation, and call them back.
